lessons.title: Using Context Clues
lessons.concept: Fill-in-the-blanks questions require choosing a word or phrase that fits the meaning and tone of the sentence. Read the entire sentence to understand context, including cause-effect, contrast, time, and intent clues.
lessons.formula: Read full sentence -> infer required meaning -> eliminate options that do not fit context -> choose best fit.
lessons.worked_example: Sentence: 'Although it was raining, he went for a walk _____.' Clues 'Although' and 'raining' suggest unexpected behavior, so an option like 'anyway' fits better than 'because of it'.
mistakes: Choosing a familiar word without checking sentence meaning
Not reading the whole sentence before answering

lessons.title: Grammar and Word-Form Fit
lessons.concept: The correct option must satisfy grammar rules: subject-verb agreement, tense, articles, prepositions, and correct word form (noun/verb/adjective/adverb). Even a meaningful word is wrong if it breaks grammar.
lessons.formula: Check subject number/tense cues -> required part of speech -> article/preposition/collocation -> final choice.
lessons.worked_example: Sentence: 'She has lived here _____ five years.' Duration requires 'for', so 'for five years' is correct (not 'since five years').
mistakes: Using wrong verb form after auxiliaries/modals
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Vocabulary Precision and Collocations
lessons.concept: Some blanks test precise word choice and common collocations (natural word pairings). Consider nuance (e.g., affect/effect, accept/except in concept, or common phrases like 'make a decision', 'take responsibility').
lessons.formula: Meaning + nuance + collocation = correct choice. Prefer the word that is both semantically accurate and idiomatically natural.
lessons.worked_example: Sentence: 'The committee will _____ a decision tomorrow.' Correct collocation is 'make a decision', not 'do a decision' or 'take a decision' in many standard test patterns (context/options matter).
mistakes: Choosing words that fit grammar but not idiomatic usage

practice.question: Fill in the blank: 'She has been studying here _____ 2020.'
practice.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time (2020). 'For' is used with a period/duration.

practice.question: Fill in the blank: 'He was tired, _____ he finished the work.'
practice.explanation: The sentence expresses contrast (tired vs finished the work), so 'but' is the correct connector.

practice.question: Fill in the blank: 'Each of the students _____ given a notebook.'
practice.explanation: 'Each' is treated as singular, so the singular verb 'was' is correct: 'Each of the students was given...'

practice.question: Fill in the blank: 'The train arrived _____ time.'
practice.explanation: The standard expression is 'on time', meaning punctually/scheduled. ('In time' means early enough, which is different.)

practice.question: She has been working here ____ 2015.
practice.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time (2015) for actions continuing to the present; 'for' takes a duration (e.g. for eight years).

practice.question: The meeting was postponed ____ the heavy rain.
practice.explanation: 'Due to' introduces the cause of the postponement. 'Despite'/'in spite' require a noun phrase but express contrast (and 'although' needs a clause), which does not fit the causal meaning here.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Neither the teacher nor the students _____ present yesterday.'
questions.explanation: With 'neither/nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('students' is plural), and the time marker 'yesterday' indicates past tense: 'were'.

questions.question: He is ____ honest man that everyone trusts him.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'such + (a/an) + adjective + noun' fits: 'such an honest man'. 'So' would require 'so honest a man' (or 'so honest that...').

questions.explanation: 'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand, which fits a doubt-clarifying explanation. Vague, tedious, and hostile do not fit the positive context.
